G1_unambiguity.justification: The equivalence semantics clearly make the critical propositions synchronized exactly when they are connected by the adopted axioms, including the vacuous single-critical-proposition case.

G2_completeness.justification: All necessary input bounds, graph conditions, costs, output requirements, and edge cases are specified.

G3_faithfulness.justification: The equivalence axioms form a connected graph with exactly n−1 edges and therefore a tree, so minimizing axioms that synchronize all critical propositions is exactly the original minimum-cost subtree problem.

G4_naturalness.justification: The statement is clear and readable, though the formal-logical framing and phrase “minimally complete” feel somewhat contrived for the underlying graph problem.
